title: Fragmented session & compatibility shim patterns for polyglot streaming + tool calls + structured outputs
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Problem: existing SDKs handle streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs in ad-hoc ways per language. Customers need: 1) ability to resume long-running streamed sessions across network blips and language/runtime boundaries, 2) a clear contract for idempotent tool invocations emitted from streamed model events, and 3) backward-compatible shims so older sync-first clients can upgrade without major rewrites. This ticket proposes a set of polyglot patterns (TypeScript/Python/Go) and a minimal compatibility shim layered on top of the new streaming/tool/structured output primitives.
notes: We aim to avoid breaking changes to the public sync SDK APIs. The compatibility shim offers: - fragment tokens (resume_id) emitted in the stream metadata - idempotency keys for each tool call event - a small JSON schema negotiation handshake for structured outputs to allow graceful evolution of fields.
design_decisions: 1) Use 'fragmented sessions' (session_id + fragment_index + resume_token) rather than single continuous sockets so clients can reattach at the last confirmed fragment. 2) Tool call events are first-class stream messages with an explicit 'status' (invocation_requested, running, completed, failed) and 'idempotency_key'. 3) Backwards compatibility is achieved via a sync->async adaptor that buffers incremental structured output until a final COMPLETE message for legacy clients.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (this ticket): produce SDK examples and a lightweight shim in TS/Py/Go + update runtime server to emit resume tokens in stream metadata. Phase 2: instrument Console tracing to understand reattach patterns and failed resumptions. Phase 3: bake into SDK packages and add migration guide.
acceptance_criteria: - TS/Py/Go examples compile and run in local harness. - Stream emitted resume_token is consumable and allows reattachment to continue with no duplicate tool invocations when idempotency_key is present. - Legacy sync API adapter can reassemble incremental structured chunks into the final object and emits an event when complete.
examples_py:
# Python: resumed fragmented session and tool idempotency handling
from redwood import SDK, StreamClient

client = SDK(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))

def run_once(idempotency_key, payload):
    # local idempotent execution store
    if not seen(idempotency_key):
        execute_tool(payload)
        mark_seen(idempotency_key)

async def consume():
    resume_token = load_resume()
    session = await client.open_session({'model': 'rw-13b', 'resume_token': resume_token})
    async for msg in session.stream():
        if msg['type'] == 'resume':
            save_resume(msg['resume_token'])
            continue
        if msg['type'] == 'tool_event':
            t = msg['tool_event']
            if t['status'] == 'invocation_requested':
                run_once(t['idempotency_key'], t['payload'])
        if msg['type'] == 'structured_chunk':
            accumulate(msg['fragment_index'], msg['data'])

# compatibility shim: blocking call that waits for final assemble
def blocking_call(prompt):
    assembled = []
    # spawn the async consumer and block until 'complete' seen
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    loop.run_until_complete(consume_and_assemble(assembled))
    return ''.join(assembled)
risks: - Complexity: session fragmentation increases state to track. We mitigate by keeping resume tokens opaque and small. - Duplicate tool invocation risk if clients mis-handle idempotency keys; mitigation: server enforces deduplication window and SDK exposes helper stores. - Legacy adapter can add latency for blocking sync clients; documented trade-off and suggested incremental migration path.
testing_plan: Unit tests for per-language helpers (resume storage, idempotency store), integration tests with local runtime harness that simulates mid-stream disconnects, e2e tests validating no duplicate tool side-effects across reconnects, and performance tests measuring reconnection overhead.
next_steps: 1) Implement minimal server-side resume-token emission and idempotency header plumbing. 2) Land example adapters in TS/Py/Go packages behind feature flag. 3) Run internal dogfood with two customers (AI-native startup and Platform team) to validate ergonomics.
arch_notes: Server will add small resume token with TTL metadata and fragment index. SDKs should treat resume tokens as opaque and store with session metadata. Idempotency keys should be stable across reconnect attempts for the same logical tool request.
